items.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Carbon With Agent 'Swarm' Feature
items.summary: On November 10, Google DeepMind opened general access to Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model to date, after a two-week preview limited to vetted cybersecurity defenders. The model targets long-horizon agentic work — complex multi-step coding, scientific reasoning and security analysis — and ships via the Gemini API, AI Studio, Gemini for Business and Google AI Ultra. Google also previewed a 'swarm' mode in Antigravity that splits one prompt into a coordinated team of specialized agents. Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per output, roughly a quarter of Anthropic's Fable 5.2.
items.impact: Carbon intensifies the frontier price-performance race and signals a shift from single-model chat to orchestrated multi-agent workflows. Its cheap, phased rollout lets Google pressure rivals while keeping the most capable cyber build under controlled access.

items.title: Anthropic Kicks Off IPO Roadshow at Up to $1.4T Valuation
items.summary: Anthropic began its IPO roadshow this week, offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each and planning a Nasdaq debut under ticker 'ANT' on November 19. At the top of the range the deal values the Claude-maker at up to $1.41 trillion fully diluted, potentially one of the largest listings ever. About 20% of the offering is earmarked for retail investors, while a roughly $26 billion private placement draws Google, Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC as strategic backers.
items.impact: A successful raise would validate sky-high AI valuations and set a benchmark for the sector. Heavy insider and strategic investment signals deep confidence in frontier-model economics, even as training costs and net losses remain enormous.

items.title: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,094 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
items.summary: Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday resolved 1,094 vulnerabilities across Windows, Office, SharePoint, Exchange, SQL Server, Azure and Edge — among the largest monthly tallies on record. The batch includes CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing flaw Microsoft confirms is under active attack; opening a crafted message leaks the victim's NTLMv2 hash to an attacker-controlled server. Two further zero-click flaws (CVE-2026-116928 Windows Search RCE and CVE-2026-119958 Windows LDAP RCE) carry CVSS 9.8, and CISA added the Outlook bug to its KEV catalog.
items.impact: Enterprises must prioritize the Outlook patch and domain-controller exposure immediately; the NTLMv2 leak enables credential relay and account takeover. The sheer volume underscores how AI-assisted discovery is inflating the monthly CVE count defenders must manage.

items.title: OpenSSH 'SSHole' Auth-Bypass Flaw Actively Exploited on Alpine Linux
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-123158 ('SSHole'), an authentication bypass in OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine, to breach cloud and container hosts. A long password triggers a musl hashing error that OpenSSH mistakes for a valid match, granting passwordless login to accounts whose shadow entry is '*'. GreyNoise logged the first in-the-wild success on November 7, about 40 hours after the 10.6p2 fix shipped; post-exploitation included cloud-metadata theft and a Python C2 implant (TAC Agent). CISA added it to KEV.
items.impact: Alpine-based containers and edge devices face instant, low-effort unauthorized logins and persistence. Operators should upgrade to 10.6p2 now or disable password authentication, and hunt for rogue authorized_keys and TAC Agent artifacts.

items.title: China Adopts First Public-Interest Litigation Law, Codifying Personal-Data Abuse Suits
items.summary: On November 6, the NPC Standing Committee passed the Law on Procuratorial Public-Interest Litigation, effective January 1, 2027. The 53-article statute consolidates over a decade of practice and explicitly lets prosecutors bring civil public-interest litigation against 'personal-information processors that unlawfully process personal data and harm the rights of many individuals.' It sets out full procedures for investigation, filing, evidence and enforcement, turning a scattered statutory authorization into a unified legal mechanism for mass privacy harms.
items.impact: The law gives prosecutors a clear, standing path to pursue large-scale personal-information abuses that individuals cannot litigate alone, raising compliance risk for data-handling firms in China and strengthening collective privacy protection.
